lessons.title: Your first SwiftData model, container, context, query, and CRUD
lessons.summary: Create a local SwiftData note store. Learn which changes are still pending, when an explicit save succeeds, and how to check restart separately.
objectives: Explain the persistent model, container, and change-tracking context, then construct each.
Read with Query and explicitly save added, edited, and deleted records.
Report failed saves honestly and explain that rollback affects all pending changes in the context.
Keep memory-only fixture checks separate from disk restart and migration checks.

sections.title: Save records beyond the screen's lifetime
sections.html:
Persistence means keeping records beyond the current screen and process. Android Room gives you a familiar reason for that storage. SwiftData integrates storage and model change tracking with SwiftUI, using its own rules. A schema describes record fields. A container configures the store. A context tracks model objects and pending edits. A query reads the models the view needs. Separate those jobs before adding features. Calling a type Model does not make it an all-purpose Android ViewModel or imply that every visible change already reached disk.

This complete source targets a scratch iOS 17+ app using Xcode 15 or later. SwiftData was introduced with iOS 17 and relies on macro-capable tooling. Replace the generated App and root declarations, keeping one entry. No earlier example types are needed. All records are synthetic. This is a first local store, not a migration, cloud synchronization feature, account store or implemented company-client persistence layer.

The app uses a persistent container and explicitly disables autosave for its main context so you can study save outcomes. Its preview uses a fresh in-memory container instead, keeping visual experiments away from the app's disk store. An in-memory fixture can prove CRUD behavior in a test context but cannot prove process-restart durability.

sections.title: Describe the note's stored fields
sections.html:
A persistent model describes data managed by the store. @Model is a compiler macro that generates SwiftData support for a class. StoredNote has an explicit UUID, title, and creation Date. @Attribute(.unique) declares the identifier's uniqueness rule in this local schema. That rule does not authorize access to the note or promise every cloud backend supports the same constraint. This example does not configure CloudKit. Its goal is a small local record with an identity that does not change whenever the user edits its title.

import Foundation
import SwiftData
import SwiftUI

@Model
final class StoredNote {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var title: String
    var createdAt: Date

    init(id: UUID = UUID(), title: String, createdAt: Date = Date()) {
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.createdAt = createdAt
    }
}

struct StoredNoteRow: View {
    @Bindable var note: StoredNote
    var body: some View {
        TextField("Synthetic title", text: $note.title)
    }
}

@MainActor
struct StoreScreen: View {
    @Environment(\.modelContext) private var context
    @Query(sort: \StoredNote.createdAt) private var notes: [StoredNote]
    @State private var newTitle = ""
    @State private var status = "Edit, then explicitly save"

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List {
                Section("Add") {
                    TextField("New synthetic title", text: $newTitle)
                    Button("Add and save") {
                        let title = newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
                        guard !title.isEmpty else { return }
                        context.insert(StoredNote(title: title))
                        newTitle = ""
                        save()
                    }
                    .disabled(newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty)
                }
                Section("Stored and pending notes") {
                    ForEach(notes) { note in StoredNoteRow(note: note) }
                        .onDelete { offsets in
                            let snapshot = notes
                            for offset in offsets where snapshot.indices.contains(offset) {
                                context.delete(snapshot[offset])
                            }
                            save()
                        }
                }
                Section {
                    Button("Save pending changes") { save() }
                    Button("Discard ALL pending changes", role: .destructive) {
                        context.rollback()
                        status = "Pending changes discarded"
                    }
                    Text(status)
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Synthetic store")
            .toolbar { EditButton() }
        }
    }

    private func save() {
        do {
            try context.save()
            status = "Save succeeded"
        } catch {
            status = "Save failed; changes are still pending. Retry or discard."
        }
    }
}

@main
@MainActor
struct StoreLessonApp: App {
    private let container: ModelContainer?
    private let setupFailed: Bool

    init() {
        do {
            let value = try ModelContainer(for: StoredNote.self)
            value.mainContext.autosaveEnabled = false
            container = value
            setupFailed = false
        } catch {
            container = nil
            setupFailed = true
        }
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            if let container {
                StoreScreen().modelContainer(container)
            } else {
                Text(setupFailed ? "Store setup failed; no data was deleted."
                                : "Store unavailable")
                    .padding()
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct MemoryStorePreview: View {
    private let container: ModelContainer?
    init() {
        do {
            let config = ModelConfiguration(isStoredInMemoryOnly: true)
            let value = try ModelContainer(for: StoredNote.self, configurations: config)
            value.mainContext.autosaveEnabled = false
            value.mainContext.insert(StoredNote(title: "Demo fixture"))
            try value.mainContext.save()
            container = value
        } catch {
            container = nil
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        if let container {
            StoreScreen().modelContainer(container)
        } else {
            Text("In-memory fixture setup failed")
        }
    }
}

#Preview("Fresh in-memory store") {
    MemoryStorePreview()
}

The initializer supplies all fields for a new record. Its default UUID is created for that construction. Changing the title keeps the ID. The query sorts by createdAt, using a key path to name that field. A key path is a typed description of a property location. Equal timestamps do not establish a deterministic tie order; add a secondary rule if your product needs one. Array positions are display positions, not permanent identities for these records.

ModelContainer holds schema and storage configuration. ModelContext tracks fetched models and pending changes, and saves them to the container's store. Query supplies view data from the installed context and responds to relevant changes. Bindable exposes controls for the model's editable title. These are related integrations, but an updated query display is not evidence that disk saving succeeded.

sections.title: Supply the store before the view reads it
sections.html:
A container is SwiftData's holder for schema and storage setup. The app creates one at its app boundary. Its modelContainer modifier supplies the context environment used by StoreScreen and Query. A preview that directly constructs the screen still needs this dependency. MemoryStorePreview creates a separate container configured to keep data only in memory, inserts its fixture, and explicitly saves that fixture. It provides a complete local host for the preview without using the app's disk store. Checking that preview therefore answers a different question from relaunching the disk-backed app.

Store setup can fail, so ModelContainer construction can throw. This app catches that error and displays a setup-failure message. It does not delete the old store to force startup through. A product needs a fuller diagnostic and recovery policy, but even this small example keeps failure separate from success. Avoid using try! as a substitute for that policy. A declared schema can compile while opening or creating the actual store still fails at runtime.

The container's mainContext is the main-actor UI context used here. Its managed models belong to that context and access contract. Do not pass them into arbitrary background tasks or share that context across isolation boundaries. For larger async work, use a suitable separate context or model-actor design and transfer safe record IDs or value snapshots. A snapshot is copied data, rather than the managed object itself. The persistence deep dives cover those choices. This first CRUD exercise deliberately uses one UI context so save and rollback scope stay easy to inspect.

sections.title: Add, read, edit, and delete with a save rule
sections.html:
CRUD means create, read, update, and delete. Add and save trims the draft, rejects blank input, inserts a new model, clears the field, then tries to save. Query may display that inserted object while it is still pending. The status records whether save completed; visibility alone is not the evidence. On failure, this example keeps changes pending. Save pending changes lets the user retry. That stated policy explains why a note can remain visible even when its durable save has not succeeded.

Query supplies the sorted records for reading. StoredNoteRow's Bindable field edits title directly in the context. Because autosave is disabled, the user must choose Save pending changes for an explicit commit. These are live edits, not separate per-row transactions. Deletion first captures the displayed objects, marks the selected ones for deletion, then saves. This list is unfiltered. If you add search, apply lesson 077's visible-ID mapping before changing the source.

A context save can include all its pending changes, not just the one row whose button was pressed. That matters when several editors share it. This beginner screen exposes one small context and explicitly labels pending changes. For independently cancellable editors, stage input or isolate the transaction scope instead of assuming each TextField is a separate database transaction.

sections.title: Handle pending changes and failed saves honestly
sections.html:
Pending means a change is tracked in memory and has not yet been committed under this save policy. A failed save can leave visible inserts, edits, or deletes in that state. Retry attempts to save those pending changes again. Rollback discards all pending changes in this context. That whole-context scope is why the button says Discard ALL pending changes. It is not a private undo for only the row beside it. If several editors share the context, an invisible rollback could discard another editor's unsaved work.

Autosave is a separate policy that may be appropriate for another application, but it should not replace understanding fallible saves and transaction ownership. Our explicit-save baseline makes the distinction observable. A successful save supports a local persistence claim under that container; a restart experiment must still verify the actual store location and the launched product. Preview saving to memory does not create durable evidence.

Schema changes, relationships, migrations, uniqueness conflicts, multiple accounts and store protection require additional design. Do not change fields in a deployed store and assume every existing record migrates safely. No such migration is performed here. The repository has its own persistence architecture; this first SwiftData example teaches an adjacent API without claiming the client already uses it.

sections.title: Check memory, save, and restart separately
sections.html:
A durability check asks whether saved data remains after its memory owner is gone. First check CRUD in a known memory fixture: add, edit, save, read, delete, and save. For a stronger same-store check, create another context from the same container and fetch after saving. That reduces reliance on one context's pending display. A disk-restart check is separate: launch the disk-backed app, save a note, preserve its sandbox, stop and relaunch, then look for the saved ID and title. Clearing app data would destroy the state needed for that experiment.

Exercise Discard with an unsaved title edit and observe the model reverting, then explain its whole-context effect. To test failure, inject or configure a bounded failure fixture and record its actual cause; don't claim that every constraint violation always throws in the same way. The lesson supplies the failure-handling path but does not fabricate a failed disk write.

The verified address model anchor demonstrates an observable in-memory model and a computed currentAddress projection. That is a useful contrast: its annotation is Observable, not Model, and the read-only source does not establish a SwiftData store. The native companion's persistence implementation and build evidence belong to its author. Your handoff should label this snippet as conceptual/type-checked as actually verified, and reserve app-run, restart and migration claims for executed checks.

quiz.explanation: Visible observation and persistent commit are different.

quiz.question: What does this rollback action affect?
options: All pending changes in this context
quiz.explanation: Its scope is the context, so unrelated unsaved editors can be affected.

quiz.question: Why use an in-memory preview container?
options: It isolates synthetic preview records from the disk store
quiz.explanation: An in-memory save is not durability evidence.

exercise.solution:
For creation, construct the model, insert it into the context, then save. Query reads records. A bound title edit changes the tracked model, then explicit save commits under this example's rule. Deletion marks the model for removal, then save commits. Before saving, the visible Query can reflect pending changes. Save succeeded means the container committed this context's pending changes. Save failed leaves them pending under the stated policy. Rollback discards the full pending context state, so it must not be described as undoing only one row.

For a meaningful store check, save the fixture, create another ModelContext from the same container and fetch StoredNote with FetchDescriptor. Verify the expected title and ID there, then delete and save and confirm absence through a fresh fetch. That is stronger than looking at the existing row alone, but an in-memory container still cannot prove restart durability. Perform the disk check separately if available, without clearing data. The preview's host constructs a fresh memory store each time, and setup failure shows a message rather than deleting data. No migration, cloud synchronization or company store modification is included in this worked answer.

This example disables autosave; other configurations can have different save policies. A memory-only preview cannot prove restart durability.

lessons.title: Capstone: test and debug a complete synthetic feature
lessons.summary: Build a small plan flow with one shared draft. Check its rules with controlled model tests, try the UI separately, and report only observed results.
objectives: Build a complete practice flow with editing, topic choice, Review, Reset, and an async suggestion.
Test when Review is allowed, how Cancel and Reset behave, and why old results cannot replace current ones.
Put app, unit-test, and UI-test source in their correct targets.
Write a handoff that separates supplied examples from checks you actually ran.

sections.title: Write the feature's rules before testing
sections.html:
A behavior contract says what the feature must do after specific input. This capstone builds a small practice plan with a display name, optional topic, reminder, picker, Review, Reset, and asynchronous suggestion. Asynchronous means the result can arrive later while other events happen. You already deliver Android features with state and user outcomes; now connect the SwiftUI pieces into one explainable flow. Use made-up data. The app is a first end-to-end exercise, not a production booking flow or evidence of a company migration.

The complete app source targets iOS 17+ with Xcode 15 or later. Create a scratch iOS App product named SwiftUICapstone and use that Swift module name for the supplied unit-test import. Replace the generated entry/root types with the app source, keeping one entry. Include a unit-test target and a UI-test target through the template or Xcode's Add Target workflow. App source belongs only to the app target; the test declarations belong only to their respective test targets.

Review requires a meaningful trimmed name and a chosen topic. Choosing a topic commits that choice to the shared draft. Cancel preserves the previous topic. Returning from Review preserves the root's edits. Reset clears the draft fields and invalidates suggestion work. Only the latest name request may publish a suggestion or error. These are the feature's invariants, rules it must preserve through allowed actions. Reminder is a practice value and schedules nothing. This capstone has no persistence; add lesson 083's store only as a separate extension with its own save contract.

sections.title: Keep one draft and supply the suggestion service
sections.html:
An owner creates and keeps the chosen model instance. Here root State owns one MainActor-isolated observable PlanDraft. The picker receives that reference and changes topic only when a topic button is activated. Cancel just requests dismissal. Review reads the same draft, so returning needs no copy-back step. LocalSuggestion is the supplied fixture service. Its Suggesting protocol describes an asynchronous operation that can throw. any Suggesting holds a service that follows that protocol. Supplying the service makes the work boundary visible instead of hiding a production client in the view.

import Foundation
import Observation
import SwiftUI

enum PracticeTopic: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case reading = "Demo reading"
    case exercises = "Demo exercises"
    var id: Self { self }
}

@MainActor
protocol Suggesting {
    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String
}

@MainActor
struct LocalSuggestion: Suggesting {
    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(200))
        return "Synthetic suggestion for \(name)"
    }
}

@MainActor
@Observable
final class PlanDraft {
    var name = "" {
        didSet { if name != oldValue { invalidate() } }
    }
    var topic: PracticeTopic?
    var reminder = false
    private(set) var token = UUID()
    private(set) var suggestion = ""
    private(set) var errorMessage: String?

    var canReview: Bool {
        !name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty && topic != nil
    }

    func invalidate() {
        token = UUID()
        suggestion = ""
        errorMessage = nil
    }

    func reset() {
        name = ""
        topic = nil
        reminder = false
        invalidate()
    }

    func load(service: any Suggesting) async {
        let expected = token
        let input = name
        guard !input.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else {
            return
        }
        do {
            let value = try await service.suggestion(for: input)
            guard token == expected, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            suggestion = value
            errorMessage = nil
        } catch {
            guard token == expected, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            suggestion = ""
            errorMessage = "Synthetic suggestion failed"
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct TopicPicker: View {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss
    let draft: PlanDraft

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List(PracticeTopic.allCases) { topic in
                Button(topic.rawValue) {
                    draft.topic = topic
                    dismiss()
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Choose demo topic")
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) {
                    Button("Cancel") { dismiss() }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct PlanRoot: View {
    @State private var draft = PlanDraft()
    @State private var showTopics = false
    let service: any Suggesting

    var body: some View {
        @Bindable var editable = draft
        NavigationStack {
            Form {
                TextField("Demo name", text: $editable.name)
                    .accessibilityIdentifier("nameField")
                Toggle("Demo reminder", isOn: $editable.reminder)
                Button(draft.topic?.rawValue ?? "Choose topic") { showTopics = true }
                NavigationLink {
                    VStack(spacing: 16) {
                        Text(draft.name)
                        Text(draft.topic?.rawValue ?? "No topic")
                        Text(draft.suggestion)
                    }
                    .padding()
                    .navigationTitle("Review")
                } label: {
                    Text("Review")
                }
                .disabled(!draft.canReview)
                .accessibilityIdentifier("reviewLink")
                Text(draft.suggestion)
                if let message = draft.errorMessage { Text(message) }
                Button("Reset") { draft.reset() }
                    .accessibilityIdentifier("resetButton")
            }
            .navigationTitle("Synthetic plan")
            .sheet(isPresented: $showTopics) { TopicPicker(draft: draft) }
        }
        .task(id: draft.token) { await draft.load(service: service) }
        .onDisappear { draft.invalidate() }
    }
}

@main
@MainActor
struct SwiftUICapstone: App {
    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { PlanRoot(service: LocalSuggestion()) }
    }
}

#Preview("Local fixture") {
    PlanRoot(service: LocalSuggestion())
}

Name changes invalidate the previous token immediately. The root's task awaits the model operation directly. Success and error handlers both check the current token and cancellation before assigning screen state. Reset invalidates even if name was already empty, so old waiting work cannot gain permission after clearing. Cancellation is a request for cooperation. The token guards are a separate rule and still matter if a service finishes old work after that request.

The preview supplies the local fixture explicitly and never constructs a production client. It uses a small delay to make interaction observable, not to coordinate tests. The App's module name is a target/product setup detail: if you choose another module, change the test import accordingly. A visible file with the wrong membership cannot satisfy the testing contract.

sections.title: Choose the completion order in model tests
sections.html:
A unit test checks model rules with explicit assertions. Put this source in the iOS 17+ unit-test target hosted by the practice app. XCTest is Apple's testing framework used here. The first test checks whether Review is allowed and what Reset clears. The second uses start expectations, signals that requests began, and continuations, handles for resuming waiting work. It releases A1, B, and A2 in a chosen order. The query sequence A → B → A shows why comparing text alone cannot tell which A request is current.

import XCTest
@testable import SwiftUICapstone

@MainActor
final class ControlledSuggestion: Suggesting {
    private var nextID = 0
    private var pending: [Int: CheckedContinuation<String, Error>] = [:]
    var onStart: ((Int) -> Void)?

    func suggestion(for name: String) async throws -> String {
        let id = nextID
        nextID += 1
        return try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
            pending[id] = continuation
            onStart?(id)
        }
    }

    func finish(_ id: Int, with result: Result<String, Error>) {
        guard let continuation = pending.removeValue(forKey: id) else {
            XCTFail("Missing or already finished request")
            return
        }
        continuation.resume(with: result)
    }
}

enum TestFailure: Error { case synthetic }

final class PlanDraftTests: XCTestCase {
    @MainActor
    func testEligibilityAndReset() {
        let draft = PlanDraft()
        draft.name = "   "
        draft.topic = .reading
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.canReview)
        draft.name = "Demo Ada"
        draft.reminder = true
        XCTAssertTrue(draft.canReview)
        draft.reset()
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.name, "")
        XCTAssertNil(draft.topic)
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.reminder)
        XCTAssertFalse(draft.canReview)
    }

    @MainActor
    func testOldSuccessAndErrorCannotReplaceNewA() async {
        let draft = PlanDraft()
        let service = ControlledSuggestion()
        let started0 = expectation(description: "A1 started")
        let started1 = expectation(description: "B started")
        let started2 = expectation(description: "A2 started")
        service.onStart = { id in
            switch id {
            case 0: started0.fulfill()
            case 1: started1.fulfill()
            case 2: started2.fulfill()
            default: XCTFail("Unexpected extra request")
            }
        }

        draft.name = "A"
        let a1 = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started0], timeout: 2)
        draft.name = "B"
        let b = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started1], timeout: 2)
        draft.name = "A"
        let a2 = Task { await draft.load(service: service) }
        await fulfillment(of: [started2], timeout: 2)

        service.finish(2, with: .success("Current A2"))
        await a2.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        service.finish(0, with: .success("Old A1"))
        await a1.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        service.finish(1, with: .failure(TestFailure.synthetic))
        await b.value
        XCTAssertEqual(draft.suggestion, "Current A2")
        XCTAssertNil(draft.errorMessage)
    }
}

ControlledSuggestion deliberately keeps waiting even if cancellation is requested. The test therefore exercises the freshness guard with actual old completions. On the normal path, every started request is released, and every Task is awaited. A fuller harness must also drain pending requests if setup fails or a timeout occurs. Otherwise waiting continuations can remain unfinished. The two-second timeout bounds a missing start signal; it does not choose which request finishes first. The explicit finish calls choose that order.

These tests are authored examples, not a claim they ran. Use Product → Test with the app scheme's test action and a compatible simulator. Record failures, toolchain and destination. Add a separate invalidation-only test and old-error-for-A1 variation when extending the suite. Do not add tests merely counting body evaluations; test the behavior the user relies on.

sections.title: Try the launched interface as a separate check
sections.html:
A UI test operates the launched app rather than calling the model directly. Put this block in the UI-test target. It types a name, chooses a topic, opens Review, returns, and resets. waitForExistence waits for a named UI condition instead of sleeping for a guessed delay. Accessibility identifiers provide machine-facing names for locating controls. The topic labels here are fixed English fixture text. A localized suite should give those choices stable identifiers too. The test's observations concern interface behavior, a different layer from the model assertions.

import XCTest

final class PlanFlowUITests: XCTestCase {
    func testChooseReviewReturnAndReset() {
        let app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launch()
        let name = app.textFields["nameField"]
        XCTAssertTrue(name.waitForExistence(timeout: 5))
        name.tap()
        name.typeText("Demo Ada")
        app.buttons["Choose topic"].tap()
        app.buttons["Demo reading"].tap()
        app.buttons["reviewLink"].tap()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars["Review"].waitForExistence(timeout: 5))
        app.navigationBars["Review"].buttons.element(boundBy: 0).tap()
        app.buttons["resetButton"].tap()
        XCTAssertEqual(name.value as? String, "Demo name")
        XCTAssertFalse(app.buttons["reviewLink"].isEnabled)
    }
}

The sample's back-button lookup and empty-field placeholder expectation reflect a simple English simulator fixture. Inspect the actual accessibility hierarchy and adjust those queries for the chosen runtime; do not report a passing UI test just because the source compiles. Model tests cannot prove tap routing, keyboard obstruction, modal gesture behavior or VoiceOver order. UI automation also does not replace assistive-technology inspection and adaptive layout checks.

Add a manual Cancel sequence with an existing topic and verify preservation. Test a long name, large text and a narrow window. For work lifetime, leave the relevant root scope during a controlled request and distinguish task cancellation from publication rejection. Never use real personal data to make the app look realistic.

sections.title: Trace the state or setup that failed
sections.html:
A derived rule calculates its answer from current fields. If Review stays disabled, inspect both the trimmed name and optional topic that form canReview. If typing fails to update it, trace the binding and shared model reference. If Cancel clears a topic, inspect the picker's action. If Reset leaves an old suggestion, inspect invalidation and both completion handlers. Reproduce old-success and old-error cases with the completion gates before changing delays. This makes the failure an explainable state transition instead of a race you hope no longer happens.

If tests cannot import the app, check the Swift module name, test host and membership. A unit-test file compiled into the app target cannot simply import XCTest and become a test bundle. If UI queries fail, inspect runtime accessibility identifiers and hierarchy. If a preview fails, verify its explicit dependencies and compile diagnostics before assuming the app cannot launch.

The active booking demo's project manifest declares separate app, unit-test and UI-test targets, providing verified evidence for those distinct products. Its dependencies and deployment minimum are checkout facts, not requirements to copy into SwiftUICapstone. The company client remains read-only. The companion at labs/SwiftUIWorkbench provides an isolated app and widget target with inspectable source. Check its README and actual target membership before using a component in the capstone.

sections.title: Report what you checked and what remains
sections.html:
A handoff lets another engineer repeat your checks and continue the work. Include the feature rules, who owns each state, sample data, minimum iOS, module name, and source membership in each target. Then state actual results. Source review, compiler checking, a linked build, simulator Run, model tests, UI tests, assistive interaction, and disk restart are separate checks. Mark any unperformed check pending. A passing related repository test cannot prove this app's behavior. The capstone also has no store, so a process-restart draft is outside its current contract.

For this capstone, the ownership map is root → one draft; picker and review → that reference; root-associated task → injected suggestion service; token → permission to publish; no store → no process-restart draft. It is intentionally bounded so the learner can explain every boundary. Advanced coordinators, bridge integration, migration and production service adapters remain the earlier core and deeper tracks.

Finish by identifying one failure you reproduced or one check still unperformed, the evidence needed next and the smallest responsible change. That makes the work useful for review and continued learning. Course attendance and a working synthetic feature do not certify exhaustive platform expertise. A clear, tested behavior contract is a practical first iOS delivery milestone.

exercise.solution:
Start with the eligibility and Reset model checks. In the gated test, A2 publishes Current A2. Later A1 success is ignored, and the old B error cannot replace that value or set the error. The token names the request generation independently of the text. ControlledSuggestion intentionally ignores cancellation while waiting so those late paths really run. Extend the design with an invalidation-only check and an old A1 error. A complete test harness must finish all waiting requests even if setup fails.

The UI sequence should end with an empty name and disabled Review under the supplied English fixture, but query details must match the actual runtime hierarchy. Cancel with an existing topic must preserve it because no cancel action assigns topic. A final note should list actual test command/action, destination, outcome and unresolved failures. If only source type checking was possible, state that; linking, Run and interaction remain pending. No persisted draft, company source change or real request is part of this capstone. Compare with the SwiftUIWorkbench companion using its actual source and recorded verification; a build result does not establish app interaction.

simple.story: Lin makes one plan card for a reading club. Ada writes her name and chooses a topic on that card. A review window shows the same card rather than another copy. If Ada opens the topic chooser and cancels, the old choice stays. Reset erases the card's fields. Lin also requests suggestions with numbered tickets so an old delivery cannot fill a cleared card. Before handing it over, they check both the card's rules and whether someone can actually reach and use each button. Those checks answer different questions.
simple.meaning: The capstone joins one shared observable draft, a picker, a Review view, Reset, and a token-guarded service. Model tests check state rules and controlled completions. UI tests check interaction through the actual app hierarchy.

example.before: PlanDraft holds name = Demo Ada, topic = reading, and reminder = true. canReview is true. A suggestion request using its current token is still waiting.
example.change: Call Reset while the older suggestion request is still waiting.
example.after: name is empty, topic is nil, reminder is false, suggestion is empty, errorMessage is nil, and canReview is false. Reset changes the token, so a later completion from the old request has no permission to refill suggestion or errorMessage.

simple.boundary: A physical card does not run asynchronous code. The tokens guard UI publication; they do not prove a remote operation stopped. Model tests do not prove tap routing, layout, VoiceOver behavior, or persistence. This capstone keeps the draft only in memory.
